name: Stereo & Depth Estimation
description: Depth-based point cloud analysis: colorize by depth, filter by depth range. Foundation for stereo vision and 3D reconstruction from camera images.

theory.overview:
Stereo vision reconstructs 3D structure from camera views. The fundamental relationship between depth $Z$, disparity $d$, focal length $f$, and baseline $B$ is:
$$Z = \frac{f \cdot B}{d}$$

A 3D point $\mathbf{X} = (X, Y, Z)^T$ in world coordinates projects to pixel $(u, v)$ via the camera intrinsic matrix $K$:
$$\begin{pmatrix} u \\ v \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{Z} K \mathbf{X}, \quad K = \begin{pmatrix} f_x & 0 & c_x \\ 0 & f_y & c_y \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

For point cloud analysis, depth-based operations include colorization by Euclidean distance and depth-range filtering for region-of-interest extraction.

depth_colorization.title: Depth Colorization
depth_colorization.content:
**1. Value**
Each point is coloured by its z coordinate (not its distance from the origin): $v_i = z_i$, which equals the depth only in a camera frame whose z axis is the optical axis.

**2. Normalization and Colormap**
The values are normalised to $[0, 1]$ over the cloud and mapped through the selected colormap (0=jet, 1=viridis, 2=plasma, 3=turbo).

depth_filter.title: Depth Range Filter
depth_filter.content:
**1. Quantile-Based Filtering**
The filter keeps the points whose z coordinate lies between two quantiles of the z distribution:
$$P_{\text{keep}} = \{p_i : Q_z(q_{\min}) \leq z_i \leq Q_z(q_{\max})\}$$
where $q_{\min}, q_{\max}$ are `min_depth` and `max_depth` as fractions (0-1). They are quantiles, not depths: the defaults (0.1, 0.9) keep about 80 % of the points whatever the geometry.

parameters.name: min_depth
parameters.description: Lower quantile of z (fraction 0-1), not a depth.

parameters.name: max_depth
parameters.description: Upper quantile of z (fraction 0-1), not a depth.
